Title: Amherst College Access to Amherst (A2A)
Summary: All-expenses-paid campus visit giving high-achieving high school seniors an authentic preview of liberal arts education, student life, and admissions at Amherst.
Eligibility_Tags: High School Seniors, Underrepresented / First-Generation Students

Title: Bowdoin College Explore Bowdoin
Summary: Fully funded overnight program where prospective students attend classes, meet faculty, interact with current students, and experience life on the Maine campus.

Title: Carleton College Taste of Carleton (TOC)
Summary: Generously funded travel program introducing prospective seniors from underrepresented cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds to Midwest liberal arts excellence.

Title: Dartmouth College Indigenous Fly-In Program
Summary: Specialized campus immersion program designed to connect Native American, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian students with Dartmouth's vibrant Native community, faculty, and academic resources.
Eligibility_Tags: High School Seniors, Indigenous / Native Students

Title: Dartmouth College Dartmouth Bound
Summary: Fully funded July campus program for rising seniors from underserved, first-generation, low-income, or rural backgrounds to experience Dartmouth firsthand.
Eligibility_Tags: High School Seniors, First-Gen / Low-Income / Rural

Title: Williams College Windows on Williams (WOW)
Summary: All-expenses-paid fly-in program providing high-achieving seniors from low-income and underrepresented backgrounds a glimpse into tutorial-style learning and rural New England campus life.

Title: Pomona College Perspectives on Pomona (POP)
Summary: Travel grant supported weekend introducing high school seniors to Southern California's premier liberal arts institution, campus dining, and consortium opportunities.
Deadline_or_Dates: Application deadline Aug 10, 2026; decisions by early September

Title: Swarthmore College Discover Swarthmore (DS)
Summary: All-expenses-paid program offering prospective seniors opportunity to attend classes, stay in residence halls, and gain insights from admissions officers.

Title: Tufts University Voices of Tufts: A Day on the Hill
Summary: One-day diversity program with no overnight stay, offering students an introduction to Tufts and its community; a virtual option is also available.
Deadline_or_Dates: Oct 18, 2026 (in-person, one day); virtual option Sept 27; application deadline July 27, 2026

Title: Washington University in St. Louis WashU FLI-In
Summary: Fly-in program for first-generation and limited-income prospective students to experience WashU (replaces the discontinued Preview WashU program).

Title: Colgate University Colgate in Focus (CIF)
Summary: Overnight visitation program offering fully funded travel for prospective seniors to engage with student organizations, faculty, and academic departments.
Deadline_or_Dates: October 2026; application deadline early September (verify exact dates — Colgate's page was showing stale cached dates as of last check)

Title: Middlebury College Discover Middlebury
Summary: Fully funded fly-in opportunity focusing on prospective students from underrepresented background interested in language immersion, environmental studies, and liberal arts.

Title: Oberlin College Oberlin Overnight (Diversity & Access)
Summary: All-expenses-paid visitation program showcasing Oberlin College and Conservatory for high-achieving high school seniors.
Deadline_or_Dates: Oct 11–13, 2026 (also a November session); priority deadline ~late September

Title: Wesleyan University WesExplore
Summary: Transportation assistance and housing assistance for high school seniors exploring open-curriculum studies and interdisciplinary majors in Connecticut.
Deadline_or_Dates: Application opens May 1; deadline Aug 3, 2026; program Oct 4–6, 2026

Title: Colorado College Discover Colorado College (DCC)
Summary: Travel assistance for prospective students to visit Colorado College and experience their unique Block Plan system.

Title: MIT Weekend Immersion in Science & Engineering (WISE)
Summary: A free, three-day fly-in for rising seniors to experience life as an MIT student, including staying on campus with a current MIT undergraduate. MIT covers all transportation costs. The program strongly encourages students from underrepresented/underserved backgrounds, rural areas, low socioeconomic means, or who would be first-generation college students to apply.
Deadline_or_Dates: Program Oct 4–6, 2026 (application deadline TBD — check site)
Eligibility_Tags: High School Seniors, Underrepresented / Rural / First-Gen / Low-Income (must attend high school in the U.S. or a U.S. territory)

Title: Lindy Waters III Foundation — Pathways: College Readiness & Career Exploration for Native Youth
Summary: A free, ongoing mentorship and college-exposure program specifically for Native youth, including one-on-one mentorship, virtual workshops, and funded campus visits (past visits include NYU, Stanford, USC, and Oklahoma State). Run by the Lindy Waters III Foundation with support from a Running Strong for American Indian Youth Dreamstarter Grant.
Deadline_or_Dates: Ongoing/rolling — cohort-based, check site for current opportunities
